newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melb up, brokers say no takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melb up, brokers say no takeover talk.

text.p: Shares in the Bank of Melbourne Ltd jumped nearly eight percent but brokers said the rise in the regional bank's price was not linked to any takeover talk.
At 1.15 p.m. (0315 GMT), Bank of Melbourne shares were 60 cents or 7.36 percent up at A$8.75 with more than 140,000 shares traded.
Bank of Melbourne is one of Australia's most touted takeovers targets due to the rationalisation among the nation's regional banks.
"There doesn't look like there is anything in it," said Mick Coombes a broker at Macquarie Equities.
"It looks like private client buying with the number of brokers that are in there," Coombes said.
BNP Equities' John Bowie-Wilson said Bank of Melbourne shares are one of the most volatile as there are always takeover rumours surrounding the Melbourne-based bank.
St George Bank Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp have been tipped by analysts as possible suitors for the Melbourne-based bank.
